mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 318i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 318i engine replacement typically costs £900-£6,500 for the engine alone, depending on condition (used, reconditioned or rebuilt) and which engine code your car has. Fitted prices through a specialist add £650-£910 in labour, while main dealer fitting can be 30-50% higher. Used 318i engine: £900-£1,800. Reconditioned 318i engine: £1,500-£3,200. Rebuilt 318i engine: £2,800-£6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 318i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a metallic rattling or ticking noise from the engine on cold start, which may quieten as the engine warms up. As the chain tensioner and guides wear further, you may notice a persistent rattle that doesn't disappear when warm, loss of power or hesitation under acceleration, engine management light illumination, low oil pressure warning (caused by broken guide debris blocking the oil pickup), or in worst cases, the engine cranks but fails to start (chain has jumped or snapped). If you hear any of these sounds on your N43- or N46-equipped 318i, have it inspected immediately - a caught-early chain replacement costs £745-£1,200 at a specialist, while a snapped chain often writes off the engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 318i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends entirely on your car's condition and value. For a 2004-2008 E90 318i worth £2,000-£6,000, a used engine (£900-£1,500) is often the most cost-effective route, but ensure the replacement has documented timing chain history. For a 2007-2011 E90 LCI 318i worth £3,000-£8,000, a reconditioned engine (£1,800-£3,200) offers a good balance of cost and reliability. For a 2015+ B48-equipped 318i worth £8,000-£18,000, a rebuilt engine (£4,500-£6,500) with a 12-month warranty is a sound investment that preserves the car's value and reliability. Always compare the cost of replacement against the car's current market value before committing.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 318i and 320i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrols in most generations, but the 320i produces more power - typically 156-184 hp versus the 318i's 118-156 hp. In the N43 generation (2007-2011), the 318i uses the N43B20A (143 hp) while the 320i uses a higher-tune variant of the same engine. The B48 generation (2015-2019) sees the 318i at 156 hp and the 320i at 184 hp. The 320i also typically commands a higher used value, making engine replacement more economically viable on older examples.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 318i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 318i engine replacement takes 8-12 hours of workshop time for a specialist, spread across 1-2 working days. This covers removal of the old engine, transfer of ancillary components (turbo on B48, injectors, sensors, wiring loom), installation of the replacement unit, and full system testing. Main dealers may take longer due to higher workload and more rigorous checklists. Supply-only orders (without fitting) typically dispatch within 1-3 working days.

mainEntity.name: What's the BMW 318i N43 timing chain replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: If caught early (before the chain jumps or snaps), a specialist can replace the N43 timing chain, tensioner, guides and all consumable bolts for £745 including VAT. The same job at a BMW main dealer typically costs £1,800-£2,500. If the chain has already jumped or snapped, the repair cost rises significantly - often £1,500-£3,000 at a specialist - and a full engine replacement may be more cost-effective. Crucially, ensure the sump is dropped to remove any broken guide debris; skipping this step risks oil starvation and subsequent engine failure.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 318i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 318i has served as the entry-level petrol option in the 3 Series range across multiple generations, offering BMW's signature rear-wheel-drive handling with accessible running costs. Over its production life, the 318i has seen four distinct engine families - from the M43 to the N42, N46, N43 and finally the B48 - each bringing incremental improvements in power, efficiency and emissions compliance. The N43 introduced direct injection, while the B48 represented BMW's modular engine architecture with significantly improved reliability.

milestones.description: 2001 - M43B19 (19 4E 1), 1.9L petrol, 118 hp - E46 318i, the final evolution of BMW's M40/M43 family
2005 - N42B20A, 2.0L petrol, 143 hp - E46 318i, introduced Valvetronic variable valve lift
2008 - N46B20B, 2.0L petrol, 129-150 hp - E90 318i, Valvetronic with improved emissions
2011 - N43B20A, 2.0L petrol, 143 hp - E90/E91 318i (LCI), BMW's first direct-injection four-cylinder petrol in the 3 Series
2019 - B48B20A, 2.0L petrol, 156 hp - F30/F31 318i (LCI), modular engine with twin-scroll turbo, improved reliability and efficiency

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 318i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 318i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 318i is a capable and popular entry-level petrol 3 Series, but its N-series engines - particularly the N43 and N46 - have well-documented timing chain vulnerabilities. The earlier M43 is relatively robust, while the later B48 represents a significant step forward in reliability. Most 318i replacement enquiries centre on the N43B20A and N46B20B, where timing chain guide failure can be catastrophic and often makes replacement more cost-effective than repair. Rebuilt 318i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 318i N43/N46 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner and plastic guide rails degrade over time. On the N43, the plastic chain guides can break up, with debris blocking the oil pickup strainer in the sump and triggering a low oil pressure warning. On the N46, the guide rails can shatter, causing the chain to jump a tooth and putting the camshafts out of alignment. Cold-start rattle is the primary early warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides and all consumable bolts - sump drop recommended to remove debris
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early; cold-start rattle only, no loss of power

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip engine, replace damaged valves/guides, clean oil system
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has jumped but not snapped; still expensive

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has snapped or engine is seized; often most cost-effective

problems.recommendation: If you catch the cold-start rattle early on an N43- or N46-equipped 318i, the preventative timing chain replacement (£745-£1,200 at a specialist) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Crucially, insist on having the sump dropped to remove any broken guide debris - skipping this step risks oil starvation and engine failure shortly after repair. If the chain has already snapped or the engine is seized, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safer bet - particularly given that second-hand N-series engines may carry the same design flaws.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N43B20A BMW 3 Series 318i engine prices

problems.h4: Valvetronic System Failure - BMW 3 Series 318i N42/N46
problems.rootCause: The Valvetronic system uses an eccentric shaft to vary valve lift continuously. The eccentric shaft sensor (also known as the Valvetronic motor position sensor) can fail, causing rough idle, stalling, and intermittent misfires. On the N46, the Valvetronic motor itself can fail, with some owners disconnecting it temporarily to keep the car driveable.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Clean eccentric shaft sensor and reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: First step; may resolve if carbon-contaminated

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace sensor and recalibrate Valvetronic system

problems.recommendation: Valvetronic issues are rarely engine-destroying on their own, but they can cause driveability problems that make the car unpleasant to use. Start with a diagnostic scan to confirm the fault code - if it's sensor-related, cleaning and recalibration often resolves the issue. If the motor has failed, replacement is straightforward for a BMW specialist and far cheaper than an engine swap.
